data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The safest protocol is a monotonic per-problem state machine with a durable checkpoint journal; it must durably record each state transition entry comprising problem ID, from-state, to-state, timestamp, and process nonce.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Journal truncation or archival moves the decision window, losing recent transitions.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"A software bug allows an invalid transition (e.g., Assigned \u2192 Reclaimed when an EvidenceCommitted entry exists but is unread due to I/O error).","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Concurrent reclamation agents race on the CAS, causing a double-assignment rather than displacement.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Each problem ID has a canonical state drawn from a partially ordered set: {Unassigned, Assigned, EvidenceCommitted, Reclaimed}. State transitions are guarded by a compare-and-swap against the durable journal tail. A process acquires a workspace only by appending Assigned. Evidence completion appends EvidenceCommitted. Reclamation is permitted only by appending Reclaimed, and only if the current tail is Assigned\u2014not EvidenceCommitted. Because the journal is the single source of truth and Reclaimed cannot follow EvidenceCommitted, completed evidence is never silently displaced. New work requires a new problem ID or an explicit reset transition, never a blind overwrite.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
